Modular Reikland Line Infantry

Reikland Line Infantry are the professional career soldiers form Reikland province of the Empire, they are volunteery and very well discipline unit. These soldiers are the main units that Reikland provides to the Empirium, other provinces can also request or hire them from the governing body of Reikland.

In the regiment there are three ranks, Riflemen, NCO, Sergeant and ceremonial rank Drummer.

My idea behind this is to modernized old Empire Hand Gunners, now they use armor and bolt action rifles. Company captains are now officers, Lords are now generals shooting their black powder revolvers instead of the flintlock pistols. Scale is very close to the old minis.

Hollowed and supported on chitubox for your printing convenience. Please enjoy and I'll be happy for your feed back

I had to go far away from dwarves for some times and I decided to start some models for the High Elf Army. Many models we can find on website are either PLA friendly and ugly or Resin printer made and beautiful.

I worked on a very well known resin model to extract whatever I could use and complete with other stuff. Heads are printed separately and the result is quiet nice. It permits to give some randomness to the unit. Hopefully, High Elf Armies are somehow very strict in their appearance and uniforms (like in the Lord of the Rings in which Elves even move at the same time in a coherent ballet).
Swords need some works with sandpaper or stuff like that for a better shape result as they are very thin.

The whole unit was hard to paint because of the tiny details everywhere but it deserved a clean treatment.

PS: the standard is handmade.

These 15 player character models are collected from various free posts we've made over the years, and come with character record sheets for our [CRUX roleplaying system, which is available as a free download from our own site](http://www.illgottengames.net/cruxuniversalroleplaying), as well as rules for [Pocket-Tactics](http://www.illgottengames.net/pocket-tactics) (our 3d pint-and-play strategy board game) and [Open-Tactics](http://www.illgottengames.net/opentactics) (our open-source, miniatures-agnostic wargaming rules).

All models are supplied without bases and print 100% support free. Daring Delvers are scaled for standard miniature gaming (30mm scale), and 15mm versions are included as well! Blank bases are included for both scales and, if you want a quick tutorial on adding them before printing, [check out this video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HGCwjUJVZ-0).

For those of you thinking about [supporting us on Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames?fan_landing=true), our patrons get special weekly model releases, access to new storefront releases and our entire back catalog, plus licensing options to sell printed versions of our designs.

To escort the Grail Reliquary, we needed some fanatic pilgrims. I wanted them to look like religious cultists, with some serious gesture and some stuff for in-battle devotions. I had in mind the picture of fat friars and fighter-monks in dresses and I wanted to be able to customize each minis but with a unique body basis.

The body I did has a very neutral standing which allows many custom stuff like a staff, a standard, a scroll, a sword, a club and of course, a shield. You can use any heads of my bretonnian set on it (the archers' hooded one, the errants' hairless one or even any of you own). For the picture, I did many pilgrims using legit heads, printed heads and even a greenstuff made head). The stuff used to custom is mainly handmade with toothpicks, greenstuff or comes from legit kits.

A body takes 1h15 to be printed.

We at Ill Gotten Games are big fans of the [Vintage RPG Podcast](https://www.stitcher.com/podcast/unwinnable-3/the-vintage-rpg-podcast), and after designing a model for Hambone [the hammer-wielding ranger, Johan](https://www.thingiverse.com/thing:3483772)), I made one for Stu as well. This is Greel, an opportunistic (but deep down, gold-hearted) ex-mercenary company leader/current warlock with a magic ring that can turn him into a tree at the first sight of danger. The model prints without support.

If you haven't checked it out, Hambone and Stu (Horvath, from [unwinnable.com](https://unwinnable.com/)) do a weekly podcast where they discuss tabletop games, and do deep dives into RPGs old and new. This all branches off of Stu's excellent [Instagram feed](https://www.instagram.com/vintagerpg/?hl=en), which is always an insightful read if you're into the history and current state of tabletop roleplaying games. We're proud to be [supporting them on Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/vintagerpg/overview), and you should really check out what they're doing/throw them some bones if you like it as much as we do.

Starting today, we're launching "Monster Mondays," a regular feature where we upload a new monster miniature design to our online [storefront](http://www.illgottengames.net/products/?category=Miniatures), with our [Patreon supporters](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames) getting free access. Each unique character will include RPG rules for our own D6Modular system (currently in beta for our patrons) and rules compatible with 5E Dungeons & Dragons.

First up, we're including Baymara, the Grand Chronicler of High Hivald. Though not technically a monster, she'll be the narrator of our growing monster compendium, and you can consider this "entry zero." (We'll be posting the first official monster entry to Thingiverse later today.) As with all of our upcoming monster designs, Baymara prints without need of support on FDM printers.

For those of you supporting us (or thinking about supporting us) on [Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames), our patrons get special access to our store releases as they come out (not to mention license options to sell printed versions of our designs).

Enjoy!

-Character art is by the talented [Benjamin Honeycutt](https://www.artstation.com/benhoneycutt)

This character was modeled for our sci-fantasy tabletop RPG, [Wayfarer: Things Beyond Wonder](http://www.illgottengames.net/wayfarer/) and for [Wayfarer Tactics](http://www.thingiverse.com/thing:1227640). If you want to print a 28mm scale version, just scale it up by 166.6%. Get a start on your 3D-printed fantasy army!

We've set up a [Patreon page](https://www.patreon.com/illgottengames) for anyone who's interested to help fund us so we can keep making free and open sourced games like Pocket-Tactics, Wayfarer Tactics. and others, not to mention the growing catalog of gaming miniatures that you can use for whatever you want!
